subproblem.title: The image of an open ball under a C¹ map is Borel and has finite H^n measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be a C¹ map, c ∈ ℝ^n and r ∈ ℝ. Then the image g(B_r(c)) of the open ball, which is empty if r ≤ 0, is a Borel subset of ℝ^P, and H^n(g(B_r(c))) < ∞, where H^n = μHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (c : Euclid n) (r : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → MeasurableSet (g '' ball c r) ∧ μHE[n] (g '' ball c r) ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 8 of the parent proof, i.e. properties (ii) and (iii) of the pieces N_k = g_k(B_{r_k}(c_k)), in the setting of Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–66).
- That lemma's proof uses that C¹ maps are Lipschitz on each closed ball.
- The measure bound is Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.8(i): H^m(f(A)) ≤ (Lip f)^m H^m(A). The book notes that this part of the argument is valid even if A is not H^m-measurable.
Notation: H^n = μHE[n], which equals Lebesgue measure L^n (volume) on ℝ^n. B_r(c) is the open ball and closedBall(c, ρ) the closed ball; both are empty for negative radius.

1. (Exhaustion of the open ball.) For t ∈ ℕ put ρ_t := r − 1/(t + 1). Then B_r(c) = ⋃_{t∈ℕ} closedBall(c, ρ_t).
- If |y − c| < r, the Archimedean property gives t with 1/(t + 1) < r − |y − c|, so |y − c| ≤ ρ_t.
- Conversely, |y − c| ≤ ρ_t implies |y − c| < r.
2. ((ii) Borel.) Hence g(B_r(c)) = ⋃_t g(closedBall(c, ρ_t)).
- Each closed ball of ℝ^n is compact (Heine–Borel), and g is continuous, being C¹.
- So each g(closedBall(c, ρ_t)) is compact, hence closed in the metric space ℝ^P, hence Borel.
- A countable union of Borel sets is Borel, so g(B_r(c)) is Borel.
3. (g is Lipschitz on the ball.) closedBall(c, r) is compact and convex.
- Dg is continuous, so it is bounded on this compact set, say ‖Dg(y)‖ ≤ Λ there.
- By the mean value inequality on the convex set, |g(a) − g(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b| for all a, b ∈ closedBall(c, r).
- In particular g is Λ-Lipschitz on B_r(c) ⊆ closedBall(c, r). If r < 0, both sets are empty and the claim is trivial.
4. ((iii) Finite measure.) By Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i), applied to g restricted to B_r(c), H^n(g(B_r(c))) ≤ Λ^n H^n(B_r(c)), where H^n on the right is the measure on ℝ^n.
- On ℝ^n, H^n = μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure.
- B_r(c) is bounded, so L^n(B_r(c)) < ∞.
- Hence H^n(g(B_r(c))) ≤ Λ^n L^n(B_r(c)) < ∞. ∎

proof_key_steps: B_r(c) = ⋃_t closedBall(c, r − 1/(t+1)), by the Archimedean property.
g is continuous, so each g(closedBall) is compact, hence closed and Borel. The countable union g(B_r(c)) is therefore Borel.
g is C¹ on the compact convex set closedBall(c, r), so it is Λ-Lipschitz there (bounded derivative plus the mean value inequality).
By Simon 2.1.8(i), H^n(g(B_r(c))) ≤ Λ^n H^n(B_r(c)) = Λ^n L^n(B_r(c)) < ∞.

audit.reason: Closed-ball exhaustion proves Borelness. Compactness and convexity give a finite Lipschitz constant, and the normalized Hausdorff image bound proves finiteness. The argument covers every real radius and zero-dimensional spaces without requiring injectivity.
